event_description: Wildfire on and around the Hanford Reservation, City of Richland, Benton County.
Wildland fire damage and suppression.
Wildfires that burned over 40,000 acres and endangered more than 350 homes in Chelan, Okanogan, Spokane and Yakima counties.
Severe storms beginning November 21, 2001 damaging homes, businesses, utilities and infrastructure (Mason and Whatcom counties were added by the February 12, 2002 amendment).

Severe storms with rain, landslides and flooding that damaged transportation infrastructure in King, Yakima, Cowlitz, Snohomish, Kittitas and Walla Walla counties. The scanned order carries the date January 8, 2002 in error; the October 10, 2003 termination dates it February 12, 2003.
Heavy winds, rain, floods and mudslides causing major flooding and road closures in Clallam, Skagit and Whatcom counties.
Winter storm and ice damage in Clark and Skamania counties.
Statewide wildfire emergency.
Storm front with wind, heavy rain, mountain snow and high tides causing flooding, mudflows and landslides in 12 counties.
Statewide emergency for storms since mid-December 2005 causing flooding, ground failures and shoreline erosion; rescinds the January 12, 2006 proclamation.
Storms January 27 to February 4, 2006 with strong winds and record rain causing flooding and landslides in 11 counties.
Flick Creek wildfire threatening Stehekin, Chelan County.
Statewide emergency for high wildfire danger from weather and fuel conditions.
Rain and wind storms with flooding and landslides beginning November 2, 2006 (rescinded and replaced November 9).
Rain, flooding, landslides and wind storms beginning November 2, 2006 in 24 counties; rescinds the November 6 proclamation.
Windstorm and heavy rain with localized flooding on December 14 to 15, 2006 in 17 counties.
Windstorm damage in Chelan, Douglas, Grant, Island, Jefferson, King and Snohomish counties (dated from the April 2, 2008 termination; the proclamation itself was not readable).
Flooding, landslides and mudslides from above-normal rainfall since November 2006, Skamania County.
Statewide wildfire emergency from high weather and fuel-related fire risk.
Pacific frontal storm causing flooding, landslides, high winds and road closures.
Severe winter storm with heavy snow in 15 counties.
Flooding from unusually warm temperatures melting above-normal mountain snowpack in six counties.
Statewide wildfire emergency from high fire risk and active fires in Eastern Washington.
Flooding and high winds November 3 to 12, 2008 with road damage and landslides in 10 counties.
Flooding from storms in western and central Washington, November 3 to 12, 2008, with high winds in southern Washington; adds Thurston and Chelan counties.
Statewide severe winter storm with blizzard conditions, record snow, freezing rain and ice.
Extreme rainfall January 11 to 17, 2010 causing landslides, rock falls and washouts in Chelan, Jefferson, King and Okanogan counties.
Severe winter storms December 8 to 18, 2010 with snow, wind and heavy rain, flooding, landslides and avalanches in 17 counties.
Severe winter storm January 9 to 26, 2011 with flooding, high winds, landslides and power outages in 17 counties.
Wildfire spread by a severe windstorm on February 12, 2011 (White Swan), Yakima County.
Severe spring storms March 15 to April 10, 2011 with high winds, flooding and landslides in seven counties.
Spring storms from May 9, 2011 with heavy rain and snowmelt flooding and landslides in 14 counties.
Statewide winter storm with heavy snow and road closures.
Storms February 17 to March 16, 2012 with strong winds, heavy rain and landslides in Clark and Mason counties.
Severe storms since July 13, 2012 with high winds, thunderstorms and extreme rainfall causing flooding and landslides in 16 counties.
Wildfire burning since August 13, 2012 in Kittitas and Yakima counties.
Statewide wildfire emergency from dry fuels and forecast lightning.
Wildfires east of the Cascade crest from dry fuels, heat and wind.
